description:
I'm interested in telling the story of some or all of the equipment that are used in the NASA space missions no matter on the Moon, Mars and elsewhere. 

Decided to make an interactive website that is about a digital musuem for the story of the equipments used in NASA space missions.
summary:
This project aims to help students learn about NASA's past space missions through pictures, timelines, and interactive activities. We developed an interactive learning library that introduces spacecraft, rovers, landers, and other equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in space.

Many students are not familiar with past space missions, and scientific information can be difficult to understand because of complex words and numbers. Our project presents this information using pictures, simple descriptions, and interactive content. Users can learn about each mission's purpose, achievements, and the equipment left behind.

This project makes learning about space more interesting and easier to understand. It also helps students discover the stories behind past missions and develop a greater interest in space exploration and science.
details:
The Spacebound Library is an interactive digital museum that is designed to share stories about space exploration equipment that has completed its mission or become inactive on the Moon and Mars. Our project provides an interactive museum where the user can explore the robots and learn about their missions and achievements. Besides that, users can browse different space missions with their mission timelines, such as when they start launching and when the mission ends. Also, it is organized into chapters for each mission, including the title and description. So, users can explore what they want to know. Through this approach, the project transforms historical and scientific information into an accessible and engaging digital learning experience.


The main benefit of The Spacebound Library is that it makes space exploration history easier for the public to understand and appreciate. Firstly, it provides a basic understanding for school-aged people about the history of the robots used by NASA for astronomy missions.

Secondly, it raises awareness of the scientific contributions made by inactive spacecraft and equipment. Even though these machines have stopped operating, the information they collected continues to support scientific research and future exploration.

Third, the project encourages curiosity about astronomy, technology, and space science by presenting information through interactive, visual content rather than relying entirely on lengthy text.


The intended impact of this project is to preserve the history of space exploration and ensure that the achievements of inactive space equipment are not forgotten.

We hope to encourage users to recognize that every space mission has a story, including its challenges, discoveries, and eventual ending. By engagingly presenting these stories, the project aims to increase public interest in space science and inspire younger generations to explore careers and opportunities in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM).

In addition, the digital museum provides a centralized platform for accessing information about historical space missions, making scientific knowledge more accessible to a wider audience.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software

  • HTML: To structure the website and organize its content.
  • CSS: To design the website layout, color, typography, and visual appearance.
  • JavaScript: To implement interactive features and improve user engagement.
  • Vite: Optimizes code and assets for production, ensuring visitors enjoy fast load times and smooth navigation through the digital museum.
  • Supabase: Used as the backend service and database platform to store, manage and retrieve project information. It can support the website by providing a centralized database for mission details and other relevant content. Depending on the implemented features, it can also provide authentication and backend services.
  • GitHub: To manage and store the project's source code.

Project creativity
The creativity of The Spacebound Library comes from presenting space exploration history from a different perspective. Space exploration is often celebrated through successful launches, major discoveries, and ongoing missions. However, less attention is given to the machines that remain on other celestial bodies after their missions end.

Our project shifts the focus towards these forgotten robots and turns their histories into an interactive digital museum. Instead of simply listing mission facts, users can explore the complete journey of each robot, from its launch and scientific achievements to its final communication or planned mission ending.

The project also highlights that not every mission ends in failure. Some spacecraft lose communication unexpectedly, while others are deliberately decommissioned after completing their scientific objectives. Presenting these different endings helps users understand the realities of space exploration. By combining storytelling, historical information and interactive website design, The Spacebound Library offers a creative way to preserve and communicate scientific knowledge.



Factor that our team consider
Information Organization: We organized mission information into clear categories, timelines and chapters to make historical content easier to navigate.

Visual Presentation: Images, illustrations and other visual materials help users understand the equipment and make The Spacebound Library more engaging.

Scientific Accuracy: We use information from reliable sources, especially NASA, to ensure that mission histories, scientific discoveries and mission endings are presented accurately.

User Experience: We aimed to create a simple and understandable interface so that users with different levels of scientific knowledge can explore the website easily.

Accessibility: As a web-based platform, the project is intended to be accessible through common internet-connected devices without requiring specialized equipment.

Copyright and Data Sources: We considered the appropriate use and attribution of NASA images, mission information and other external resources.
